items.title: Amara Raja Just Opened a 500 Crore Battery Plant in Telangana
items.summary:
Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies has opened a ₹500 crore customer-qualification plant at its Telangana Giga Corridor, part of a wider ₹9,500 crore, 16-gigawatt-hour factory programme that takes its phase-one investment past ₹1,500 crore. The facility will validate lithium-ion cells with automotive and industrial clients from August 2026, ahead of its 2-gigawatt-hour commercial plant, Giga One, going live next year. 

In this episode of Front Page, we break down why chairman Jayadev Galla is building operational experience before committing to full-scale lines, and how a second Telangana corridor in Mahabubnagar plans a further ₹10,000 crore in cell and pack capacity. Does India's battery push succeed by moving fast to commercial scale, or by proving itself first at plants like this one?

items.title: BYD's New Patent Uses AI Cameras to Check Under Parked Cars
items.summary:
BYD has filed a patent for an underbody vision system that uses cameras and AI to check for people, pets, or animals hiding beneath a parked car before the engine starts, comparing before-and-after ground images to flag anything that has changed. It pairs with a separate radar patent that detects children or pets left inside the cabin, covering both blind spots at once.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down how the two-step scan cuts false alarms from shadows and debris, and why this is one piece of a sensing ecosystem BYD is building across nearly every blind spot on its vehicles. 

Is this the start of a genuinely safer parking lot, or a sign that cars are carrying more sensors than they need?

items.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Just Cracked a NIST Quantum Encryption Finalist
items.summary:
Anthropic's unreleased Claude model has quietly dismantled a top-three finalist in the US government's search for quantum-safe encryption, cutting its key strength in half using a multi-agent AI workflow that ran mostly without human cryptography experts. The same system then broke a weakened round of AES-128 roughly 200 to 800 times faster than the best human record, though the full 10-round cypher securing today's internet remains intact. 

In this episode of Front Page, we break down how Claude found a hidden mathematical symmetry in the Hawk encryption candidate, invented a new attack technique on AES, and why Anthropic disclosed everything to NIST before going public. Is AI-assisted cryptanalysis now the biggest wildcard in the race to secure the post-quantum internet?
